en: Udāna 7.1 Paṭhamalakuṇḍakabhaddiyasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the Venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya with a discourse on the Dhamma in many ways.
Then, as the Venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya was being instructed by the Venerable Sāriputta with a discourse on the Dhamma in many ways...
As he was being instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by the discourse,
his mind was liberated from the taints through non-clinging.
The Blessed One saw that the Venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya’s mind had been liberated by the Venerable Sāriputta through many methods.
Being instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened by a discourse on the Dhamma,
his mind was liberated from the taints through non-clinging.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
thus liberated, he has crossed the flood.”
“Untrodden before, for the sake of non-renewal of existence.
